title: Dolbeault complexes are acyclic resolutions
statement:
Let $M$ be a Hausdorff second-countable complex manifold of finite dimension on each component. Let $\mathcal O_M$ be its sheaf of holomorphic functions, $\Omega_M^p$ its sheaf of holomorphic $p$-forms, and $\mathcal A_M^{p,q}$ its sheaf of smooth complex differential forms of type $(p,q)$, with negative-degree sheaves zero. In holomorphic coordinates write $d=\partial+\bar\partial$ for the type decomposition of exterior differentiation; these operators commute with restriction and satisfy $\bar\partial^2=\partial^2=\partial\bar\partial+\bar\partial\partial=0$. For every $p\geq0$, the inclusion $\Omega_M^p\hookrightarrow\mathcal A_M^{p,0}$ gives an exact augmented cochain complex [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of sheaves of $\mathbf C$-vector spaces
$$0\longrightarrow\Omega_M^p\longrightarrow\mathcal A_M^{p,0}\xrightarrow{\bar\partial}\mathcal A_M^{p,1}\xrightarrow{\bar\partial}\cdots.$$
Every $\mathcal A_M^{p,q}$ is acyclic for global sections: $R^r\Gamma(M,\mathcal A_M^{p,q})=0$ for $r>0$, computed in sheaves of $\mathbf C$-vector spaces. The same assertion holds for a finite disjoint union of such manifolds of different dimensions, and for the empty manifold. On holomorphic functions $\partial=d_{\mathrm{hol}}$ is the holomorphic exterior derivative.

source.place: WANTED locally: Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, I §3.E Lemma (3.29), printed pp.28--29; IV §6 Example (6.13) and formulas (6.14)--(6.16), printed p.216; type decomposition in I §2. Read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf. These are resolution and acyclicity inputs, not a cohomological comparison with algebraic forms.

proof.text: In a holomorphic chart use the basis $dz_I\wedge d\bar z_J$. For a coefficient $f$, $df=\sum_j f_{z_j}dz_j+\sum_j f_{\bar z_j}d\bar z_j$, so exterior differentiation has just the two type components stated. A holomorphic change of coordinates replaces the $dz_j$ by holomorphic linear combinations of the new $dz_j$ and the $d\bar z_j$ by their conjugates; the chain rule therefore preserves type and these two components glue. The coordinate formulas are local, hence commute with restriction and are complex-linear. By [lem-sfb-chart-exterior-derivative-square-zero], applied at each point to the real chart with complex-valued forms, $d^2=0$ (a form on a chart can be extended arbitrarily away from a neighborhood of the point). Its separate type components on a $(p,q)$-form are $\partial^2$, $\partial\bar\partial+\bar\partial\partial$, and $\bar\partial^2$; each is zero. For a holomorphic function $f$ the antiholomorphic derivatives vanish, and $\partial f=\sum_j f_{z_j}dz_j=d_{\mathrm{hol}}f$.

source.place: I §3.C, formulas (3.13)--(3.16), printed pp.23--24; I §1.A, exterior differentiation

proof.text: In degree zero write a smooth $(p,0)$-form as $\sum_{|I|=p}dz_I\, f_I$. Its $\bar\partial$ is $(-1)^p\sum_I dz_I\wedge\bar\partial f_I$. The independence of the coordinate wedge basis shows that this vanishes exactly when every $\bar\partial f_I$ vanishes. The degree-zero assertion of [lem-sfb-local-scalar-dolbeault] says precisely that these coefficients are holomorphic. Thus the kernel sheaf at degree zero is $\Omega_M^p$; its inclusion into smooth forms is injective since it is the inclusion of the same coefficient functions. This also shows that the augmentation is killed by the differential.

source.place: I §3.C Cauchy--Riemann criterion; I §3.E, Lemma (3.29)(a), printed pp.28--29

proof.text: For $q>0$, near any point write a $\bar\partial$-closed $(p,q)$-form uniquely as $\alpha=\sum_{|I|=p}dz_I\wedge\alpha_I$ with scalar $(0,q)$-forms $\alpha_I$. The coordinate formula gives $\bar\partial\alpha=(-1)^p\sum_I dz_I\wedge\bar\partial\alpha_I$, hence every $\alpha_I$ is closed. Apply [lem-sfb-local-scalar-dolbeault] to these finitely many coefficients and intersect their primitive neighborhoods. Choose $\beta_I$ there with $\bar\partial\beta_I=\alpha_I$. Then $\beta=(-1)^p\sum_I dz_I\wedge\beta_I$ satisfies $\bar\partial\beta=\alpha$. Consequently every kernel section is locally an image. By [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], cokernels are sheafifications of sectionwise cokernels, so this local surjectivity says exactly that the kernel modulo the image sheaf is zero. Together with steps 1--2 this proves exactness of the augmented cochain complex in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: I §3.E, Lemma (3.29)(b), printed pp.28--29; IV §6, Example (6.13), printed p.216

proof.text: Multiplication of each coefficient of a smooth $(p,q)$-form by a smooth complex-valued function gives $\mathcal A_M^{p,q}$ a unital $\mathcal E_M$-module structure commuting with restrictions. The underlying real manifold satisfies the Hausdorff, second-countability, and local finite-dimension hypotheses of [lem-sfb-smooth-function-modules-acyclic]. That theorem gives $H^r(M,(\mathcal A_M^{p,q})_{\mathrm{ab}})=0$ for $r>0$. Apply [lem-pe-ringed-site-derived-evaluation-slice] to the small site of opens of $M$, its terminal object $M$, and the constant sheaf of rings $\mathbf C_M$. Its modules are exactly sheaves of complex vector spaces: locally constant scalars act by constant multiplication locally and these actions glue. Enough injectives for this ringed space is [lem-sc-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. The comparison theorem identifies the underlying additive group of $R^r\Gamma$ in those complex sheaves with the abelian-sheaf cohomology just shown to vanish. A complex vector space whose additive group is zero is zero, proving the requested acyclicity in the stated category.

source.place: IV §4, Corollary (4.19), printed p.205; IV §6, Example (6.13), printed p.216; coefficient comparison: Stacks Tags 03FD, 03F3, 01DI

proof.text: All local arguments use only the dimension of the chart in question. If $p$ or $q$ exceeds that dimension, the relevant wedge space is zero, and the same arguments apply with empty coefficient families. For dimension zero the augmentation identifies functions with holomorphic functions and every positive-degree form is zero. A finite disjoint union of the stated manifolds is again Hausdorff and second-countable and has exactly those local charts, so the preceding argument applies without a common dimension. For the empty manifold every sheaf of complex vector spaces has zero sections on its only open set; all terms, cohomology groups, and asserted identities are zero. No passage from exactness of sheaves to exactness of the complex of global forms has been asserted.

lean.statement: theorem dolbeault_acyclic_resolution (M : Type u) [TopologicalSpace M] [T2Space M] [SecondCountableTopology M] (A : Atlas M) : ∃ (D : DolbeaultSheafData A) (sq : ∀ p q : ℤ, D.dbar p q ≫ D.dbar p (q + 1) = 0), (∀ p q : ℤ, D.del p q ≫ D.del (p + 1) q = 0) ∧ (∀ p q : ℤ, D.dbar p q ≫ D.del p (q + 1) + D.del p q ≫ D.dbar (p + 1) q = 0) ∧ (∀ p : ℕ, ∃ i : (HomologicalComplex.single (ComplexSheaves M) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).obj (D.omega p) ⟶ CochainComplex.of (D.smooth p) (D.dbar p) (sq p), (HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf (V := ComplexSheaves M) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0 (D.omega p)).inv ≫ i.f 0 = D.inclusion p ∧ QuasiIso i) ∧ (∀ (p q : ℤ) (r : ℕ), 0 < r → IsZero (((complexGlobalSections (M := M)).rightDerived r).obj (D.smooth p q))) ∧ (∀ p q : ℤ, p < 0 ∨ q < 0 → IsZero (D.smooth p q)) ∧ D.inclusion 0 ≫ D.del 0 0 = D.holomorphicDerivative ≫ D.inclusion 1
